Abstract. Let H2g+1 be the monic squarefree polynomials of degree 2g + 1 over Fq [T ], where
q is odd. Let ΘD be the unitarized Frobenius class of the quadratic L-function attached to D.
We study the fixed-distance range beyond the symplectic trace wall,

We also define the stable Euler coeﬀicient for every fixed odd prime power q. A rigorous

The closest earlier work has three strands. Entin, Roditty-Gershon, and Rudnick developed
the multiple character sums which underlie the exact transition [3]. Their estimate stops before
the total degree used here. Andrade and Keating gave the function-field ratios recipe [1]. Wang
proved the required ratios estimate for suﬀiciently large fixed q [6].
Bergström, Diaconu, Petersen, and Westerland proved fixed-coeﬀicient stability for the hyperelliptic family [2]. Miller, Patzt, Petersen, and Randal-Williams proved uniform twisted
stability [4]. Their current bounds do not sum the unstable diagonal tail in this problem.
The paper is organized as follows. Section 2 gives the explicit formula and the post-wall scale.
Section 3 extracts the target coeﬀicient from Wang’s theorem. Section 4 evaluates the four swap
terms. Section 5 computes the arithmetic correction. Section 6 proves the fixed-q convergence
of the Euler product. Section 7 isolates the remaining small-q tail estimate.

4. The four swap terms
Put x := q −α1 and z := q −α2 . We keep the four shifts distinct during differentiation. We also
use nested coeﬀicient contours. This avoids an ambiguity at the cross-poles x = z. For a monic
irreducible P , write GP and YP for the local Euler factors of the ratios-recipe main term and
of Y , respectively; thus the local factor of A is GP /YP . We denote their two formal numerator
variables by X1 , X2 and their two denominator variables by Y1 , Y2 ; the explicit local quotient is
given in Section 5.
The sum of the four swap terms is holomorphic in Wang’s region, although the individual oneswap terms have apparent poles at x = z. Start with the equal Fourier contours in Lemma 3.1,
deform the contour of the sum slightly to |z| < |x|, and only then split it into four terms. No
pole is crossed because the sum is holomorphic. Reversing the deformation gives |x| < |z| and
interchanges the two one-swap terms. Thus the total coeﬀicient is independent of the chosen
nesting.
Lemma 4.1 (analytic remainders). Fix q in Wang’s range. After the displayed zeta factors
have been removed, the arithmetic factors and all derivatives used below are holomorphic on a
product annulus
q −ε < |x|, |z| < q ε
for some ε > 0. Consequently, a term for which the displayed polar kernel does not supply every
Fourier degree tending to infinity is Oq (q −ηc ) for some η > 0.
Proof. Andrade–Keating’s product A(α; γ) converges absolutely and locally uniformly when all
shifts lie in a suﬀiciently small fixed neighbourhood of zero. Under x = q −α1 and z = q −α2 this
neighbourhood contains such a product annulus. Differentiation on a smaller compact annulus
preserves holomorphy and uniform boundedness. Cauchy’s estimate on the two boundary circles
then bounds a Laurent coeﬀicient exponentially in any index which tends to infinity. Since
k = c + ℓ with ℓ fixed, this is Oq (q −ηc ) after decreasing η if necessary.
□
